FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Fourth Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Secondary Cells and Batteries Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division 
Council. 


This standard was first published in 1960 and revised in 1972, 1984 and 1991. This revision has been carried out 
to incorporate some extra operational tests and also to change the operating parameters of the cells to accommodate 
a more global orientation to the subject specification. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1652 : 2013 


Indian Standard 


STATIONARY CELLS AND BATTERIES, LEAD-ACID 
TYPE WITH PLANTE POSITIVE 
PLATES — SPECIFICATION 


( Fourth Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard specifies rated ampere hour capacities, 
overall dimensions, performance requirements and 
tests for high discharge performance, stationary lead 
acid cells and batteries using plante type positive plates. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts 
to this standard. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 1885 (Part 8) and the following shall apply. 


3.1 High Discharge Performance Cells — Cells 
containing pure lead plante plates of lamelle type with 
pasted type negative plates. 


3.2 Type Test — Tests carried out to prove conformity 
with the requirements of this standard. These are 
intended to prove the general quality and design of a 
given type of battery. 


3.3 Acceptance Tests — Tests carried out on sample 
selected from a lot for the purpose of verifying the 
acceptability of the lot. 


3.3.1 Lot — All batteries of the same type of design 
and rating manufactured by the same factory during 
the same period, using the same process and materials, 
offered for inspection at a time shall constitute a lot. 


4 RATING AND DESIGNATION 


4.1 Ampere-Hour Rating 


The rating assigned to the cell shall be the capacity 
expressed, in ampere-hours (after correction to 27°C) 
stated by the manufacturer to be obtainable when the 
cell is discharged at the 10 h rate (C,,) to a final voltage 
of 1.85 V. 


4.2 Designation of Cells 


Cells shall be designated by the letter ‘P’ for plante 
followed by the standard rating of the cell. 


Example: 


P 40 — HDP designates a high discharge performance 
plante type stationary cell of 40 Ah capacity. 


5 CONSTRUCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 


5.1 Containers 


The containers shall be made of transparent polymeric 
material for example SAN. 


5.1.1 Containers shall conform to IS 1146. 


5.2 Cell Lids 


Lids used with sealed or closed type cells shall be of 
opaque nature made from SAN or ABS plastic material 
and shall be provided with a vent plug(s). Terminal 
posts shall be suitably sealed at the lid by means of 
rubber grommets, sealing compound or other suitable 
devices to prevent acid spray. 


5.3 Venting Device 


The venting device shall be of anti-splash type with 
more than one exit hole and shall allow gases to escape 
freely but shall effectively prevent acid particles or 
spray from coming out. 


5.4 Sealing Compound 


The sealing compound when used in sealed or closed 
cells, if bitumen based, shall conform to IS 3116. 


5.5 Plates 
5.5.1 Positive Plate 


The plante positive plate shall be of the pure lead 
lamelle type with plante formation. 


5.5.2 Negative Plate 


The plates shall be pasted construction and of good 
workmanship. 


5.5.3 The positive plate shall be hung from ledges 
moulded in the container. The negative plate shall be 
supported from the bottom of the container. 


IS 1652 : 2013 


The weight of each plate group shall be transmitted 
vertically on to a flat base. 


The clearance between the sides of the container and 
the positive plates, and between the bottom of the 
container and the positive plates, shall conform to 
Table 1. 


Table 1 Clearances Between the Container 


and Plates

iii) 100 12 40 


5.6 Separators 
The separators shall conform to IS 6071. 


5.7 Terminal Posts 


Positive and negative terminal posts, where provided 
of cells shall be clearly and unmistakably indentifiable. 
The positive terminal shall be marked with red colour 
in addition to ‘+’ marking. 


5.8 Fasteners 


Bolts, nuts and washers for connecting the cells shall 
be effectively lead-coated to prevent corrosion. 


5.9 Connectors 


Where it is not possible to bolt the cell terminals 
directly to assemble a battery, separate lead-coated 
copper or aluminium connectors of suitable size shall 
be provided to join the cells. In such cases, the coating 
shall be adequate and tenacious. In some cases, it may 
be necessary to connect individual cells in parallel as 
specified by the purchaser. In such cases, suitable 
connectors shall be used. 


5.10 Electrolyte 


The sulphuric acid and water used for preparing 
electrolyte for the cells shall conform to IS 266 and 
IS 1069. 


5.11 Spray Arrestor 


Open cells shall be provided with spray arrestors of 
adequate area over the plates. These may be of glass 
sheet of at least 3 mm thick or suitable plastic sheet 
and shall be adequately supported.

The capacities and maximum external dimensions of

each cell shall be 2 V.

7 MARKING 


The following information shall be indelibly and 
durably marked on the outside of the cell: 


a) Indicating the source of manufacture; 

b) Ampere hour capacity at 10 h rate; 

c) Upper and lower electrolyte level in case of 
transparent containers; 

d) Year of manufacture; and 

e) Country of origin. 


7.1 BIS Certification Marking 
The cells may also be marked with Standard Mark. 


7.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the rules and regulations made thereunder. The 
details of condition under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


8 PACKING 


The cells shall be suitably packed so as to avoid any 
loss of damage during transit. 


8.1 The manufacturer shall supply one copy of 
instruction manual for initial treatment and routine 
maintenance during service with every batch of batteries. 


8.2 The following information shall be provided on 
the instructions cards: 

a) Designation of cell or battery (see 4.2); 

b) Ampere-hour capacity; 

c) Nominal voltage; 

d) Manufacturer’s instructions for filling, initial 

charging; 
e) Normal finishing charging rates; and 
f) Maintenance instruction. 


9 CONDITIONS OF SUPPLY 


9.1 To facilitate procurement of correct type of 
stationary cells, it is recommended that the user should 
furnish information regarding his requirements as given 
in Annex B, at the time of enquiry or order similarly, 
the manufacturer should furnish the information given 
in Annex C. 


9.2 Other conditions of supply shall be subject to 
agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 


10 GENERAL REQUIREMENT FOR TEST 


10.1 Temperature of Test 


The temperature of electrolyte during test discharge 
shall be within the limits of 16°C and 38°C. 


10.2 Specific Gravity 


For the purpose of test requirements, the specific 
gravity of electrolyte of fully charged cell shall be 
1.215 + 0.005 corrected to 27°C. Temperature 
correction for hydrometer readings of specific gravity 
shall be made as follows: 


a) For each 1°C above 27°C, 0.000 7 to be added 
to the observed reading and; 


b) For each 1°C, below 27°C, 0.000 7 to be 
subtracted from the observed reading. 


10.3 Test Equipment 


The voltmeters, ammeters, thermometers and 
hydrometers used for the tests shall comply with the 
requirements of 10.2 of IS 8320. 


10.4 Classification of Tests 


10.4.1 Type Tests 


The following shall constitute type tests and shall be 
carried out to the sequence given below: 


IS 1652 : 2013 


a) Verification of constructional requirements 
(see 5); 

b) Verification of marking (see 7); 

c) Verification of dimensions (see 6.1); 

d) Test for capacity (see 10.6) — Test for voltage 
during discharge (see 10.11); 

e) Ampere-hour and watt-hour efficiency tests 
(see 10.10); 

f) Test for loss of capacity on storage (see 10.8); 

g) Endurance test (see 10.9); 

h) Loss of water test (see 10.12); 

j) Test for suitability for floating battery 
operation (see 10.13); and 


k) Internal resistance and short circuit test 
(see 10.14). 


10.4.2 Type test shall be carried out on three (3) cells. 
Two (2) cells shall undergo all tests except endurance 
test while the other would undergo endurance test 
preceded by a capacity test. 


For capacities above 500 Ah, however a test cell with 
suitable number of positive plates along with other 
components to be fabricated in a suitable sized 
container such that capacity does not exceed 500 Ah. 
All other tests would be carried out on two (2) cells of 
respective capacity. 


10.4.3 Acceptance Tests 
The following shall constitute the acceptance tests: 


a) Verification of marking (see 7.1); 

b) Verification of dimensions (see 6.1); 

c) Test for capacity (see 10.8); and 

d) Test for voltage during discharge (see 10.11). 


10.4.3.1 Acceptance tests shall normally be carried out 
at the direction of the purchaser. 


The date and place of testing shall be subject to 
agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 


10.4.3.2 The sampling scheme and criteria for 
acceptance for cells up to and including 600 Ah 
capacity shall be in accordance with 11.14 of IS 8320. 
For capacity more than 600 Ah, it shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 


10.5 First Charge 


The cell of battery, if received in the dry uncharged 
condition shall be filled with the electrolyte and 
charged in accordance with the manufacturer’s 
instructions. 


10.6 Tests for Capacity 


10.6.1 After standing on open circuit for not less than 
12 h and not more than 24 h from completion of a full 


IS 1652 : 2013 


charge, the cell or battery shall be discharged through 
a suitable variable resistance at constant current of 
I=0.1 Cio A. The discharge shall be stopped when 
the closed circuit voltage across the battery falls to 
1.85 x nV, where n is the number of cells connected in 
series. 


10.6.1.1 The rated capacity shall be reached within 
three discharges subsequent to the initial charge. Once 
the rated capacity has been met, further discharges for 
capacity shall be discontinued. 


10.6.2 Requirement 


The period of discharge shall not be less than 10 + 
0.09 (t — 27) h nor exceed 12 + 0.9 (t — 27) h, t being 
the test temperature, in degrees Celsius. 


10.7 Alternate Rated Test Discharge 


Test for capacity may, by agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier, be carried out at rates other 
than the 10 h rate. In such cases, the 5 h rate is 
recommended, capacities at various rates of discharge 
and corresponding final voltages are given in Table 3. 
For the purpose of acceptance, the capacity test shall 
be carried out at one rate only. 


10.8 Loss of Capacity on Storage 


10.8.1 This test shall be carried out on the two cells 
which have successfully passed the capacity test in 
accordance with 10.6. 


10.8.2 The cells shall be fully recharged at the current 
specified by the manufacturer and shall then be submitted 
to two consecutive capacity tests in accordance with 10.6, 
the value of the initial capacity ‘C being calculated as 
the mean of the two results thus obtained. 


10.8.3 After a complete recharge and the cleaning of 
electrolyte from its surface the cells shall be left on 
open circuit for a period of 28 days without disturbance 
at a temperature of 27 + 2°C. 


10.8.4 After the storage for 28 days, the cell shall be 
discharged in accordance with 10.6. The value of 
capacity measured after storage is denoted by C. 


10.8.5 The loss of capacity S expressed as a percentage 
is calculated from the following formula: 


JE x100 
C 


10.8.6 Requirement 


The loss in capacity thus measured shall not exceed 
15 percent. 


10.9 Endurance Test 


10.9.1 The test shall be made on cell, which has been 
subjected to only capacity test. No further tests shall 
be made on this sample after this test. 


10.9.2 One cell shall be subjected to an overcharging 
current of 0.1 X C,,A at a test temperature of 40 + 3°C 
for total periods of 2 000 h as given in 10.9.4. 


10.9.3 Overcharging Periods 
a) 2 cycles of 300 h charging followed by test 
discharge; 
b) 3 cycles of 200 h charging followed by test 
discharge; and 
c) 8 cycles of 100 h charging followed by test 
discharge. 


10.9.4 Throughout these periods of charge the cells

shall be immersed in a tank of water the temperature 
of which shall be maintained at 40 + 3°C. The cells 
shall be so immersed that the top of each cell is 25 mm 
above the water level in the rank. If the two cells are 
placed in the same tank, a distance between a cell and 
the sides of the tank shall be at least 25 mm. 


10.9.5 At the end of each period of charging, as 
specified in 10.9.3 (a) to (c), the cells shall be subjected 
without redrawing to a test discharge (C,9) to an end 
voltage of 1.85 V in accordance with 10.6. 


This discharge test shall be conducted without undue 
delay and without removing the cell from water batch 
and shall be made within 2 h of termination of charging 
current. If for any reason the time between the 
termination of charging and the test discharge exceeds 
2 h, the cell in water bath may, at the option of the 
manufacturer, be kept on a ‘trickle charge’ not 
exceeding I = 0.01 x C,y A until the time of test 
discharge. 


10.9.6 When the test discharge is completed, the cells 
shall be immediately subjected to the next period of 
continuous charge without any recharging. 


10.9.7 Requirement 


The cell shall give not less than 9 h of discharge of the 
final test discharge after the last period of charge. 


10.10 Ampere-Hour and Watt-Hour Efficiency Test 
10.10.1 Ampere-Hour Efficiency 


A fully charged cell shall be discharged at I = 0.1 x Cio A 
to an end voltage of 1.85 V/cell, careful calculations 
being made of the exact number of ampere-hours 
delivered. On recharge the same number of ampere- 
hours are put back at the same out-off voltage as before. 
The efficiency of the cell, is then calculated as the ratio 
of the ampere-hour delivered during the second 
discharge to the ampere-hour put in on the charge. While 
conducting the test, a minimum rest of 12 to 24 h shall 
be given between each charge and discharge. 


10.10.1.1 Requirement 


The ampere hour efficiency when calculated as 
described in 10.10.1 shall be not less than 92 percent. 


10.10.2 Watt-Hour Efficiency 


The watt-hour efficiency shall be calculated by 
multiplying the ampere-hour efficiency by the ratio of 
average discharge and recharge voltage. The values of 
discharge and recharges voltage shall be calculated 
from the log sheets for ampere-hour efficiency. 


10.10.2.1 Requirement 


The watt-hour efficiency when calculated as described 
in 10.10.2 shall be not less than 80 percent. 


IS 1652 : 2013 


10.11 Test for Voltages During Discharge 


The cell need not be discharged specially for this test. 
For the purpose of this test the voltages shall be 
obtained from the log sheets for capacity test in which 
the cell meets the rated capacity. 


10.11.1 Requirement 


The closed circuit voltage of cell shall not be below 
the values given below:

10.12 Loss of Water Test 


This test shall be done on a cell which has earlier met 
the requirement of the capacity test as per 10.6. After 
fully charging the cell as per the manufacturer’s 
instructions, it should be thoroughly cleaned and dried. 
The cell then should be weighed immediately but not 
exceeding 1 h after drying with an accuracy of 0.05 
percent or maximum least count of 10 g for the balance 
used. All the vent-cum-filling plugs should be put in 
place and closed tightly. The cell shall then be put on a 
constant voltage charging with voltage setting of 2.4 
V per cell kept in a constant temperature water bath of 
50 + 2 °C for 21 days at a stretch. After the completion 
of 21 days, the cell shall be taken out, thoroughly dried 
and weighed accurately with the least count as before. 
The difference in the initial and final weights shall be 
construed as to be the weight of the water lost during 
this period of time. The loss is then calculated based 
on the obtained Ah capacity of the cell during the C,, 
capacity discharge test. 


10.12.1 Requirement 


The water loss thus measured shall not exceed 0.4 g/ 
Ah/cell based on the obtained C,, capacity. 


10.13 Test of Suitability of Floating Battery 
Operation 


The test shall be carried out on a group of two cells 
which have qualified the capacity discharge test as 
per 10.6. 


The cells shall be kept at an ambient temperature as 
close as practically possible to the reference 
temperature of 27°C and the upper surface of the lid 
shall be kept clean and dry throughout the duration of 
the test. 


The cells shall be subjected to a constant float voltage 


IS 1652 : 2013 


as per the manufacturer’s recommendation during the 
test. The initial voltage of the cells across the terminals 
shall be measured and recorded. 


After intervals of three months the float voltage, 
specific gravity and the electrolyte level of each cell 
shall be measured and recorded. After six months of 
continuous floating operation, the cells shall be 
subjected to a capacity discharge as per 10.6. 


10.13.1 Requirement 


Cells tested as per the above procedure shall meet the 
following requirements: 


a) The electrolyte densities shall remain within 
the specified tolerance limits as recommended 
by the manufacturer; 

b) The individual cell voltages shall remain 
within the specified tolerance limits as 
recommended by the manufacturer; and 

c) After a period of six months, the obtained 
capacity on discharge according to 10.6 shall 
be at least equal to the rated capacity of the 
cell. 


10.14 Short Circuit Current and Internal Resistance 
Test 


The test shall be conducted on minimum number of 
two cells which have qualified the capacity test as

After fully charging the cells as per the manufacturer’ s 
recommendation, the cells shall be kept at ambient 
temperature and the discharge characteristics U = f(Q) 
of the cells is then established by finding out two of its 
points by the following way : 


a) First Point (U,, I) — The cells are discharged 
at a current I, = 4/,9......... 6l io A. After 20 s 
of such discharge the voltage and the current 
are measured and these values give the first 
point (U,, 1). 


The discharge shall be interrupted after 25 s 
maximum and the cells shall be kept on open 
circuit, without recharging, for 2 to 5 min 
before the second point is determined. 


b) Second Point (U,, I,) — The cells are then 
discharged at a current of I, = 20/,,........ 40/,, 
A. The voltage and current are measured after 
5 s of onset of this discharge and form the 
second point (U,, L). 


The discharge characteristic U = f(D is found by linearly 
joining the two points (U,, 1,) and (U,, Z) as in Fig. 1. 
The line can be linearly extrapolated to U = 0 V. The 
intercept indicates the short-circuit current Z.. The

gradient of the U = f(I) line.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
